docs.title: RK3588 Vision Deployment Kit
docs.text:
Skip the two-week setup. This kit is a verified ONNX → RKNN deployment pipeline for the Rockchip RK3588: converted model artifacts, a tested version matrix, per-operator CPU-fallback data, and measurements taken on real hardware — not on an emulator, not copied from a datasheet.

This documentation is free and complete. Read everything, check the numbers, run the free sample. The paid package contains the runnable artifacts, the full raw measurement data, and the tuned conversion scripts.

docs.title: Measured environment
docs.text:
All numbers on this site were measured on one documented configuration:

  • SoC / board: Rockchip RK3588
  • OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, kernel 6.1.118
  • Runtime: librknnrt 2.3.2 · Driver: rknpu 0.9.8
  • Conversion: rknn-toolkit2 2.3.2 (x86_64 host)

See the Version Matrix for the exact tested combinations, and Benchmarks for the measurement protocol. Numbers measured outside this matrix are marked as such wherever they appear.

docs.title: Why not just do it yourself?
docs.text:
You can. The official guides are free. What they don't give you:

  • Artifacts that are already verified on hardware, with SHA-256 hashes.
  • The failure records — which INT8 calibration silently collapses a detector's confidence scores, which artifact balloons to 18 MB because of a compiler memory-planning quirk, which ops fall back to CPU and by how much. See Known Issues.
  • A version matrix that is known to work as a set, instead of three days of toolkit/driver/runtime mismatch debugging.

That is what the package sells: the two weeks, already spent.

docs.title: Protocol
docs.text:
Every number below was produced the same way, on the reference configuration:

  • Warmup: 10 runs, then 50 timed runs per session
  • Sessions: 3 independent sessions, each in its own process; the reported value is the median of session medians
  • Priming: one sacrificial load + 5-run cycle in a separate process before measuring (see the first-context effect)
  • Timer: NPU PERF_RUN profiling; CPU-fallback share computed from per-operator timings
  • Verdict: NPU_ONLY = no operator executed on CPU; MIXED = some operators fell back (share shown)

Single-session numbers on this SoC can sit ~15% off the sustained state; that is why the protocol above is not optional when comparing.

docs.title: How to read this table
docs.text:
• INT8 is not automatically faster. RetinaFace INT8 is slower than its FP build on this stack and is shipped as a measurement record; the FP artifact is the recommended one. Details in Known Issues.
  • MIXED is not broken. A few Reshape operators routinely fall back to CPU with a small time share. What matters is the share, which is printed for every model — most vendor tables omit it.
  • Full raw reports (per-operator timings, memory deltas, session-level data) are in the Complete package. The summary above is complete and free; the raw files are what you re-check a procurement decision against.

docs.title: Buying
docs.text:
What exactly am I paying for, if the documentation is free? The runnable artifacts (12 converted models, FP + INT8), the conversion pipeline scripts, the worked examples, and — in Complete — the full raw measurement reports and conversion notes. The documentation is free because it is how you verify the package is real before paying.

Is there a free trial? The free sample (GitHub) is one complete model end to end — pipeline, artifacts, and data format identical to the paid kit. Together with this documentation, that is the trial. There is no time-locked demo; code does not work that way.

Refund policy 14 days: if the pipeline does not run as documented on a configuration inside the Version Matrix, after working through the self-check list and support, you get a full refund.

docs.title: Technical
docs.text:
Can I use the artifacts in a commercial product? Yes. The kit license covers commercial use of the pipeline, examples, and data. Model weights keep their upstream licenses — each artifact's origin and license is listed in LICENSES.md inside the package. Only weights with redistribution-compatible licenses (Apache / MIT / BSD) are included.

Why is librknnrt not in the package? It is Rockchip-proprietary and not ours to redistribute. The package ships sideload instructions and a version check instead.

My numbers differ from the Benchmarks page. First check the first-context effect and whether your versions match the matrix. Then compare per-session: the protocol (3 sessions, median) matters more than any single run.

Does INT8 always help? No — see RetinaFace in Known Issues. The kit tells you per model instead of assuming.

docs.title: Known Issues & Failure Records
docs.text: This page is the part you cannot get from a model zoo or an AI assistant: things that actually went wrong on real hardware, how they were diagnosed, and what ships instead. It is updated whenever a measurement contradicts a previous claim.

docs.title: First-context effect
docs.text:
The first RKNN process after the board has been idle measures ~15% slower, even after warmup runs, on RK3588 with the rknpu_ondemand governor. A single quick benchmark right after boot will systematically understate the board.

Kit protocol: one sacrificial load + 5-run cycle in a separate process before any timed session (see Benchmarks). If your numbers are ~15% below this site's and you benchmarked once, cold, this is almost certainly why.

docs.title: RetinaFace INT8
docs.text:
Two separate problems, both reproduced:

  1. Artifact bloat. The toolkit 2.3.2 build of this model produced an 18.9 MB artifact for a ~1.5 M-parameter network. Layer isolation traced it to memory planning around the final Concat operator: roughly 17.5 MB of zero-filled image is written into the artifact. It is a compiler behaviour, not a settings error, and cannot be tuned away from the user side.
  2. Confidence collapse with normal calibration. The normally-calibrated INT8 build systematically compresses detection confidence: at a 0.5 threshold it detected 0 of 3 faces in the reference scene. The KL-divergence calibrated build detects 2 of 3 at the same threshold, but remains slower than the FP build (7.99 ms vs 6.43 ms p50) with a 2.74% CPU-fallback share.

What ships: the FP artifact is the recommended RetinaFace build. The KL-calibrated INT8 artifact is included as a measurement record with this page as its documentation. The normal-calibration build was withdrawn.

docs.title: PP-OCRv4-Rec Reshape fallback
docs.text: Both FP and INT8 builds of the recognition model execute one Reshape (after the final softmax) on CPU: 2.58% / 2.61% of frame time. It does not block deployment; it is recorded so your latency budget is honest.

docs.title: Session variance
docs.text: Session medians for the same artifact can differ visibly (e.g. YOLO11n INT8 session p50 values of 23.8 / 31.4 / 31.2 ms in one measurement set). The kit reports the median of three sessions and keeps the per-session values in the raw reports (Complete package) — if a vendor table shows you one number with no spread, ask how it was measured.

docs.title: Quickstart (free sample)
docs.text: The free sample contains one complete, runnable slice of the kit: MobileNetV2 classification, FP and INT8, end to end. It exists so you can verify the pipeline, the documentation style, and the data format before spending anything.

docs.title: 1. Get the runtime in place
docs.text:
The kit does not redistribute Rockchip's proprietary runtime. Install librknnrt 2.3.2 using the vendor package for your board, then verify:

strings /usr/lib/librknnrt.so | grep -i "librknnrt version"
# expected: librknnrt version: 2.3.2

Only the combinations in the Version Matrix are tested.

docs.title: 2. Run the sample
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/anguoyang/rk3588-vision-kit-sample
cd rk3588-vision-kit-sample/example_classify_mobilenetv2
python3 run_classify.py --model ../models/mobilenetv2_rk3588_fp.rknn --image zebra.jpg
python3 run_classify.py --model ../models/mobilenetv2_rk3588_int8.rknn --image zebra.jpg

Expected output (measured on the reference board):

top-1: zebra  0.9993   (FP)
top-1: zebra  0.9993   (INT8)

docs.title: 3. Check the numbers
docs.text: Compare your board against the reference measurements in Benchmarks. On the reference configuration, MobileNetV2 measures 8.63 ms p50 (FP) and 4.15 ms p50 (INT8). A first-run result ~15% slower than that is a known platform effect, not a fault — see Known Issues.

docs.title: Rules that come from hard experience
docs.text:
Toolkit and runtime move together

Artifacts converted with toolkit 2.3.2 are verified against runtime 2.3.2. Mixing a 2.3.x toolkit with a 2.0/2.1 runtime (or the reverse) produces load errors or silent accuracy loss. The kit pins the pair.

The toolkit is x86_64 only

Conversion happens on an x86_64 host. The board only runs artifacts. The pipeline scripts in the package assume this split.

Runtime is not redistributed

librknnrt is Rockchip-proprietary. The kit ships sideload instructions and version checks, not the binary.

docs.title: Support boundary
docs.text: Support covers configurations inside this matrix. Outside it, the documentation still applies as guidance, but results are not guaranteed — start from the FAQ self-check list before contacting support.
